name: Amazon.com, Inc.
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Amazon runs the largest single-company AI-infrastructure program (~$220B 2026 capex, raised from ~$200B) and the largest corporate clean-energy portfolio on earth (40+ GW across 700+ projects, #1 per BloombergNEF since 2020, including 11 utility-scale battery projects) — with AWS re-accelerating to +36.7% growth (fastest in 18 quarters) on GW-denominated Trainium commitments from Anthropic (up to 5 GW) and OpenAI (~2 GW). BACKGROUND: Founded 1994; retail, AWS, advertising, devices, streaming, healthcare. FY2025 revenue $716.9B (+12%), net income $77.7B; AWS $128.7B with a $244B backlog (+40%). Custom silicon (Trainium3/Graviton5) is a >$25B run-rate business. The cost: trailing FCF swung from +$38.2B (2024) to negative.
ecosystemRole: We assess Amazon as the ecosystem's largest and most institutionalized energy buyer: the 40+ GW portfolio explicitly includes 11 utility-scale BESS projects — Bellefield (with AES, Kern County CA) alone targets 1 GW solar + 1 GW/4,000 MWh of storage, the largest US solar+storage build, with Phase 1 (500 MW solar + 1 GWh BESS) completed June 2025 — plus a nuclear program spanning the Talen Susquehanna PPA (ramping to 1,920 MW through 2042 after FERC blocked the behind-the-meter expansion) and X-energy SMRs (target 5+ GW by 2039). Project Rainier (~2.2 GW reported campus power) anchors the Anthropic compute buildout.

productsAndServices.name: AWS & AI Infrastructure
productsAndServices.description: The largest cloud platform: FY2025 revenue $128.7B; Q2 2026 $42.2B (+36.7%, ~$169B run rate) with $16.6B operating income (39.4% margin). Custom silicon via Annapurna Labs: Trainium3 (up to 40% better price-performance vs Trainium2; 'over 5x output tokens per megawatt'; 144-chip UltraServers at 362 MXFP8 PFLOPs) and Graviton5; chips/AI businesses each >$25B annualized run rate. Project Rainier (New Carlisle, IN — ~$11B campus, >1M Trainium chips running Claude) is described by Amazon as the world's largest AI computing cluster.
highlights: GW-denominated silicon commitments: Anthropic up to 5 GW of Trainium capacity; OpenAI ~2 GW — plus the reported $38B/7-year AWS-OpenAI agreement (NVIDIA GPU capacity)
2.1M+ AI chips deployed in 12 months; 1M+ NVIDIA GPUs planned for 2026 — Amazon buys both sides of the silicon debate
AWS backlog $244B (+40% YoY) at FY2025; the Anthropic stake produced a $53.4B pre-tax mark-up gain in Q2 2026
October 2025: 14–15-hour us-east-1 outage (DynamoDB DNS race condition) affected ~70,000 organizations — the single-region-dependency critique made real
productsAndServices.positioning: The 2024–25 'losing the AI race' narrative (AWS growing slower than Azure/GCP) reversed through 2026 as growth re-accelerated from +19% to +36.7%; still the largest base by revenue. Trainium is the most credible non-NVIDIA training silicon but with essentially one frontier anchor (Anthropic).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Cloud consumption + enterprise agreements; silicon only via AWS capacity (direct sales are unconfirmed rumor)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Trainium4 targeted 2027; ~$200B→$220B 2026 capex predominantly AWS; named state investments: PA $20B, MS $25B, NC $10B, IN $11B, GA, OH

productsAndServices.name: Energy & Storage Procurement
productsAndServices.description: 40+ GW of carbon-free capacity across 700+ projects in 28 countries; 100% renewable-matched for the third consecutive year; #1 corporate renewables buyer per BNEF since 2020. Storage: 11 utility-scale BESS projects — Bellefield (AES; 1 GW solar + 1 GW/4 GWh BESS at completion, 15-yr PPA, Phase 1 done June 2025), Baldy Mesa (CA solar+storage with AI/ML grid optimization), Primergy Nevada (600 MW solar + 600 MW BESS, May 2025), ~1.5 GW of paired BESS across CA/AZ. Nuclear: Talen Susquehanna front-of-meter PPA ramping to 1,920 MW through 2042 (restructured after FERC's 2024 rejection of the behind-the-meter ISA); X-energy anchor investment + Energy Northwest 'Cascade' SMRs (~320 MW phase one, up to 960 MW, ~2030) targeting 5+ GW by 2039; Dominion North Anna SMR exploration. Plus Zanskar geothermal (100 MW) and a broad international PPA book.
highlights: Bellefield is the flagship reference project US BESS suppliers cite — AES is the counterparty channel
The FERC ISA rejection (Nov 2024, upheld April 2025) set the national precedent against uncompensated behind-the-meter nuclear co-location — reshaping how every hyperscaler structures nuclear deals
Rate-design friction building: Ohio Consumers' Counsel FERC petition, Oregon's ~30% data-center rate increase — the cost-allocation fight follows Amazon's load
productsAndServices.positioning: Largest and longest-standing corporate portfolio; unlike Meta's tolling posture, Amazon signs paired solar+storage PPAs at scale, making it the most direct hyperscaler demand channel for BESS developers
productsAndServices.soldThrough: PPAs with developers (AES, Primergy), utility agreements, SMR JVs
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Counterparties: renewable developers, storage integrators, nuclear operators
productsAndServices.roadmap: Cascade SMR construction ~2030; Bellefield Phase 2; continuing international expansion

highlights: FTC Prime 'dark patterns' settlement: $2.5B (Sept 2025); the FTC monopoly case trial moved to February 2027

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Amazon has the most complete hyperscaler energy machine: paired solar+storage PPAs at GWh scale (Bellefield), ~2 GW of front-of-meter nuclear, SMR construction plans, and 11 named BESS projects — for storage suppliers, Amazon's developer counterparties (AES, Primergy) are the most established hyperscaler-linked channel in the covered set. Basis: BNEF rankings, project completions, first-party portfolio claims.

(High confidence) We assess the dual-silicon strategy (Trainium for Anthropic, NVIDIA for OpenAI and general capacity) hedges the central technology risk of the cycle while the equity stake in Anthropic converts compute supply into balance-sheet gains ($16.8B + $53.4B marks in two quarters) — a structural advantage no other hyperscaler currently replicates at this scale.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the FERC Susquehanna precedent Amazon triggered now defines US nuclear-for-data-center dealmaking: behind-the-meter co-location without cost allocation is dead, front-of-meter PPAs are the template — which pushes incremental firming demand toward grid-side assets, including storage.

(Moderate confidence) We assess free-cash-flow inversion is the honest cost of the program: TTM FCF fell from +$38.2B to negative territory while capex guidance rose to ~$220B — the market has accepted it while AWS accelerates; a growth stumble would reprice the entire buildout.

(Low confidence) Reports of direct external Trainium sales and of adoption beyond Anthropic (OpenAI/Apple/Uber workloads) circulate on low-authority outlets only — unverified, and partly contradicted by the NVIDIA-based OpenAI deal.

(High confidence) We assess Amazon's storage procurement splits into three layers that must not be conflated when qualifying an opportunity. Layer 1 — utility-scale BESS: Amazon signs PPAs, developers own the assets and choose the cells, so the OEM decision sits with AES (Bellefield, 1 GW/4 GWh at completion) and Primergy (600 MW Nevada), not Amazon. Layer 2 — behind-the-meter BESS at the campus: no announced Amazon deployments, a genuine structural contrast with xAI (Megapack fleet) and Crusoe (integrated energy stack). Layer 3 — rack-level BBU inside the white space, which is where AI-specific battery demand actually lands. Basis: Amazon's own renewables disclosures name developers but never battery vendors; no first-party or trade source documents an Amazon on-site BESS installation. The practical consequence: 'does Amazon buy BESS?' has no single answer — the buying center, the decision criteria, and the vendor set differ per layer.

(Low confidence) Korean and Taiwanese trade press place Samsung SDI in the Layer-3 BBU position: an April 2026 report of final-stage talks with AWS on a battery supply agreement for BBU-based UPS (~$700M, pricing the last open term), and July 2026 reporting that Samsung SDI ships BBU cells through Taiwan's Simplo with Amazon among the end customers. Neither company has confirmed either arrangement, both rest on unnamed sources, and Samsung SDI is reported in parallel talks with Meta and Google — so this is a supplier winning a slot in a supply-short market, not an exclusive win. Treat as unverified reporting and attribute it as such in any external conversation.

(Low confidence) Fluence is the intuitive guess for the Bellefield battery supplier given AES owns roughly 28% of Fluence, but we found no press release, filing, or trade coverage naming the supplier for that project. This is an untested inference from a corporate relationship, not a sourced fact — do not repeat it as one; the AES project team is the only reliable path to confirmation.

relationships.note: Developer-owner of all three campuses in the $18B northwest Louisiana program.
relationships.context: STACK develops and owns Amazon's three Louisiana campuses (Caddo Parish, Bossier Parish, Shreveport) — announced at $12B in February 2026, raised to $18B in August 2026, with STACK funding all water, wastewater and electrical upgrades. Amazon's largest named third-party development program.

relationships.note: $38B seven-year AWS compute deal — the marquee win of OpenAI's multi-cloud era.
relationships.context: November 2025: OpenAI contracted $38B of AWS capacity over seven years (hundreds of thousands of GB200/GB300-class GPUs by end-2026, expandable 2027+); April 2026 reporting adds a ~$100B eight-year expansion and AWS exclusivity for OpenAI's 'Frontier' enterprise platform (single-outlet, unconfirmed). Amazon backs Anthropic while selling compute to its rival — both sides of the frontier race run through AWS.

UPI reported a Samsung SDI battery-supply agreement with Amazon in April 2026, consistent with trade reports of direct supply talks and Amazon as an end customer of the Simplo BBU chain — none company-confirmed; tracked as an unverified upside option in the data-center power stack.

relationships.note: Multi-year 2170 cell supply to Zoox, Amazon's robotaxi unit — deliveries from early 2026.
relationships.context: November 2025: Panasonic announced a multi-year 2170 cylindrical-cell supply agreement with Zoox for robotaxis, deliveries beginning early 2026 — indirect Amazon exposure to Panasonic's cell capacity through the autonomy program.
Amazon holds a 375 MWdc Ohio PPA with Lightsource bp — part of the hyperscaler offtake roster (Google, Meta ×2, Amazon, Microsoft) attached to the #1-ranked US solar developer.

relationships.note: Portfolio investment via the Climate Pledge Fund (Series F) — plus reported last-mile deployments.
relationships.context: Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund participated in Mainspring's $258M Series F (April 2025), and the linear-generator maker's fleet section carries reported Amazon last-mile deployments — a strategic-investment relationship in FEOC-immune onsite generation.
